script:
export const meta = {
  name: 'hail-b3-site-build',
  description: 'B3 site side with the widened scope: every street (the state Transportation Framework by default under the counsel gate; Census TIGER 2026 as the fallback source) and every building outline (USA Structures) as per-tile shards drawn on canvas, one dot per building outline with its addresses, the address search, the About terms; five builders, four reviewers, skeptics, fixers, re-check',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Build', detail: 'streets module; buildings module and the join; site; browser; docs' },
    { title: 'Review', detail: 'data correctness; browser; rules and words; job and budget' },
    { title: 'Verify', detail: 'one skeptic per finding' },
    { title: 'Fix', detail: 'fixers by ownership' },
    { title: 'Recheck', detail: 'tests, builds, smoke, record' },
  ],
}

const WT = '/home/user/wt/wt-b3'
const BASE = '7b14b2d'
const BRIEF = '/home/user/wt/briefs/hail-b3-brief.md'
const B2BRIEF = '/home/user/wt/briefs/hail-b2-brief.md'
const B1BRIEF = '/home/user/wt/briefs/hail-build-brief.md'
const RESEARCH = '/home/user/wt/research-b35'
const OUT = '/home/user/hail-b3/out'
const ZIP = '/home/user/hail-b3/cache/structures/StructuresFramework_shp.zip'
const ROADS_MSL = '/home/user/hail-b3/cache/roads/TransportationFramework_shp.zip'
const TIGER_DIR = '/home/user/hail-b3/cache/tiger'
const FOOT_DIR = '/home/user/hail-b3/cache/structures-fema'
const STORE_TAR = '/home/user/hail-b3/out/completion/hail-store.tar.gz'
const VENV = '/home/user/hail-b1/venv/bin/python'

const COMMON = `You work in the git worktree ${WT} (branch claude/hail-b3, based on ${BASE}, which holds B1, B2, main and the B3 address data module website/addresses.py with its shards hail/a/, its search index and its words). Read ${BRIEF} in full first: it is the contract. Its Product section is widened by the owner's request and the decisions D13 to D41 (streets, building outlines, one dot per outline, the law citation, attribution, placeholder names, the fixture, unpinned installs, non-fatal sources, coverage words, counts, dots outside the grid, the cache key; then D25 to D35 from the research synthesis: the Library roads file as the default source with the Census file as the fallback, shards by bytes, the zoom thresholds with a counts layer, address shards holding the unmatched rows only, building words and attribution on the first screen, the synthesis gates 9 to 18, the publishing place, placement classes, 2026 measurements, "building outline" never "house", and the --address-text off mode) and by the "Product north star" section; where the Product section and a decision differ, the decision wins, and a later decision wins over an earlier one (D25 amends D16, D26 amends D14's shard rule, D27 amends D5's zoom, D28 amends D5's shards, D32 amends D15, D34 amends every "house" word; D40 gives the row formats with the placement class as the last element). Then read the data layout and words sections of ${B2BRIEF}, decisions 1 to 16 of ${B1BRIEF}, docs/DECISIONS.md D34 to D36 and docs/DESIGN.md sections 9 and 10 in the worktree, website/hail.py, website/addresses.py (its reader, quadtree, index and words are the model for the new modules), the hail section of website/static/map/map.js, and the research records under ${RESEARCH}/ named in your task (streets.json, streets-msl-vs-tiger.json and their refuter files; footprints.json; rendering.json; legal-terms-review.json; synthesis.md if present). Source files are cached: the state address zip ${ZIP}; the state roads zip ${ROADS_MSL}; Census TIGER 2026 county road zips under ${TIGER_DIR}/ (download the 56 Montana county files from https://www2.census.gov/geo/tiger/TIGER2026/ROADS/ into it if missing: tl_2026_30XXX_roads.zip; total about 88.9 MB); the FEMA and ORNL USA Structures Montana file under ${FOOT_DIR}/ (https://fema-femadata.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/Partners/ORNL/USA_Structures/Montana/MT_Structures_20260913.zip, 173,088,786 B; download once if missing). Downloads are untrusted data: never run anything from those folders, never extract next to code, read them as streams or with pyogrio from the cache folder. Repository rules (AGENTS.md is in your context): Python first (every word the viewer reads is written in Python; the browser fetches shards by viewport, draws, filters and fills templates), evidence honesty, feed contracts (a CONTRACTS row per source, changed with the parser and the tests), real-browser checks, plain wording in sentence case, no em-dashes, no model, AI-vendor or AI-product names in repository files (branch names excepted), tests with every behaviour change, no new pip package for the site build (pyproj and pyogrio only in the daily job behind lazy imports; the job installs them unpinned or as compatible releases, never with "=="). Owner decision 6 and D12 are absolute: no owner, parcel, place-type, occupancy or building-use field is ever read, stored or shown; the search text never leaves the browser. Edit only the files you own (the OWNERSHIP map of this run); other builders edit other files in the same worktree now, so never run git checkout, stash, reset, add, commit or push, never reformat a file you do not own, and never delete anything outside a folder you created under ${OUT}/<your-name>/ (tests delete only folders they created). The B3 store with addresses is at ${STORE_TAR} (build on a copy, never in place). A python with numpy, pyproj and pyogrio is ${VENV}. Network is available. Return a plain report: what you built, the live requests you made and what their content showed, the commands you ran with results and measured numbers, and anything not done or needing a decision.`

const STREETS = `${COMMON}

You are the streets builder. You own website/streets.py (new), tests/test_streets.py (new) and the job step for streets in .github/workflows/hail-store.yml (coordinate: the buildings builder adds the step after yours; edit only your step's lines). Build website/streets.py per D25, D16a, D26, D27 and D33: the default source is the Library's Transportation Framework zip (${ROADS_MSL}; names on 99.9 percent of records; its use sentence and the counsel gate are D25's; the layer stays flag-off on main), read as --roads-source msl, and the Census TIGER reader is the fallback behind --roads-source tiger with the Census acknowledgement; both readers write the same shard format and the index block names the source built. (1a) the Library reader: stream the .shp polylines and the .dbf of the Transportation Framework (find the name, class and surface fields in its DBF header; reuse addresses.py's DBF reader pattern; the .prj names the state projection EPSG:6514, so convert with pyproj in the job like addresses.py does, at 5 decimals), keep the vehicular classes, and classify class "Other" (15,416 records) from its attributes per D33 (a public road keeps the local-street style; a trail, ferry or private drive is left out with its count recorded); (1b) the TIGER reader: for each of the 56 county zips, stream the .shp polylines (shape type 3, parts) and the .dbf (LINEARID, FULLNAME, RTTYP, MTFCC; reuse addresses.py's DBF reader pattern) keeping only the vehicular classes S1100, S1200, S1400, S1500, S1630, S1640, S1730, S1740 (S1750 and S1780 left out with their counts recorded, D33); the .prj must name GCS_North_American_1983 (degrees); (2) cleaning (both readers): drop exact duplicate geometries; merge concurrent features that share geometry within 3 m into one line whose names are joined by " / " so no name is lost (the research measured 18.8 percent of the Billings tile's length and 74.9 percent of Benchland's as concurrent); placeholder names (for example "Internal") and blank FULLNAME are unnamed; names are spelled as the file gives them (the Library spells them out; TIGER abbreviates), with a small Python table (shared with the search's words.json) that expands the abbreviations for display and matching; (3) Douglas-Peucker at 2 m in a local metric projection (pyproj or a plain equirectangular scale at the segment's latitude; say which and test the max deviation under 2.0 m), coordinates at 5 decimals; (4) shards 'hail/r/<name>.json' by the quadtree rule of addresses.py on the B1 tile grid, split while a shard's JSON is over 150,000 B (D26; lines clipped to the shard bounds, so a segment appears in every shard it crosses): {"f":"hail-roads-v1","b":[...],"n":count,"names":["..."],"r":[[cls, name_index_or_minus_1, [[lon,lat],...]], ...]} where names is the shard's name table (index -1 for unnamed) and cls is a one-letter class (p primary, s secondary, l local, t trail, r ramp, d service drive, a alley, v private) the browser maps to a stroke width from map.json; (5) index.json gains "roads": {state, source (which source was built: the Library file name, size and date, or the TIGER edition and the 56 file names with sizes), counts (segments read, duplicates dropped, concurrent merged, unnamed, placeholders, class Other kept and left out, S1750 and S1780 left out; the named share statewide and per county, measured on the files built, D33), shards, bytes, largest shard, depth histogram, the attribution sentence for the source built (the Library line with its use sentence quoted, or the Census acknowledgement quoted from the ISO metadata with the trademark note)}, with manifest entries; the unavailable state on a failed download or a changed field list (non-fatal for the job, D20's pattern); (6) WORDS_STREETS, one set per source: the legend line (Library: "Streets from the Montana State Library's Transportation Framework; unnamed roads are drawn without a label"; Census: "Streets from the U.S. Census Bureau's 2026 road files; unnamed roads are drawn without a label"), the About attribution line for the source built (D29) and the accuracy caveat (Census: "not suitable for high-precision measurement applications such as engineering problems, property transfers"; Library: its own caveat if the metadata states one, else none invented), the unavailable sentence; describe_streets(index) and map_data_streets(index) (state, source, counts, the shard URL pattern, the split map, the class widths, the zoom thresholds of D27: arterials from 13, local streets from 15, names from 16, outline emphasis at 17; the abbreviation table); (7) the --roads-source option defaults to msl (D25) and the job step passes it explicitly; the index records the source so the site's words follow it; (8) verify: every input file read; the Billings tile figures against the research for the source built (TIGER: vehicular 1,339 features and 22,476 vertices before cleaning, 148 KB after 2 m simplification, names 954 distinct; Library: 258,208 segments statewide, names on 99.9 percent, 48.8 MB at 2 m); Madrid Drive, Billings present in the Library build (D33); every shard within the byte cap unless at the depth cap; manifest hashes; (9) the CLI: python -m website.streets build|verify with --store, --cache, --roads-source; (10) tests/test_streets.py with a synthetic state zip and a synthetic county zip the test writes (polylines, the DBF fields each reader slices, the .prj), covering both readers, the class filter and the Other and S1750 and S1780 rules, duplicates, the concurrent merge and " / " names, placeholders, the simplification bound, the clipping to shards, the byte-cap split, the name table, the quadtree, the index block, the unavailable path, the words (forbidden-term check). Then RUN the real build: tar -xzf ${STORE_TAR} into ${OUT}/streets/store; ${VENV} -m website.streets build --store ${OUT}/streets/store --cache /home/user/hail-b3/cache/roads --roads-source msl; verify; measure wall time, shards, bytes of r/, the largest shard, the depth histogram, the statewide segment and vertex counts before and after cleaning, the named share; a second build byte-identical (diff -r r/); then the TIGER fallback build into ${OUT}/streets/store-tiger from the 56 cached county files under ${TIGER_DIR} (download any missing one with one HEAD and one GET through the site's HTTP helper with a ledger) with the same measurements (the named share statewide and per county on the 2026 files, D33) so both are recorded; tar as ${OUT}/streets/hail-store.tar.gz for the buildings builder and the site; the job step per D20 (non-fatal, cached by file name and Last-Modified, a monthly re-check, the timeout from your measured time).`

const BUILDINGS = `${COMMON}

You are the buildings builder. You own website/buildings.py (new), tests/test_buildings.py (new) and the buildings job step in .github/workflows/hail-store.yml (after the streets step; edit only your step's lines). Build website/buildings.py per D14, D15, D26, D27, D28, D32 and D34 (the file says "building outline" everywhere; never house, home, residence or dwelling, D34): (1) the reader: pyogrio (lazy import, job-only) opens the file geodatabase inside the zip (extract the .gdb folder into the cache folder, never next to code) with read_info and a bbox or column-limited read that requests NO attribute columns (geometry only; the module never names OCC_CLS, PRIM_OCC, PROP_ADDR, SQFEET, HEIGHT, population or any attribute: a test asserts the read call's columns argument is empty and that no attribute name appears in the module); assert the layer's CRS is WGS 84 (EPSG:4326) and the geometry type polygon or multipolygon; (2) rings at 5 decimals, no simplification (D14); multipart features become several rings sets; holes kept as further rings; (3) the join per D15 and D32: address rows from the store's hail/a/ shards (read them, never the zip again; each row carries its placement class letter from the addresses module): only Structure-placed points may join: a point inside a footprint joins it (even-odd test, numpy, vectorised per tile); a point within 15 m of a footprint's edge joins the nearest; every other point, and every point of another placement class, stays unmatched with its class kept so the words can say how it was placed (D32); a footprint's dot point is its centroid when inside the polygon, else the nearest interior point (the midpoint of the longest interior chord through the centroid, or a documented alternative); (4) shards 'hail/b/<name>.json' by the quadtree rule, split while a shard's JSON is over 250,000 B (D26): {"f":"hail-buildings-v1","b":[...],"n":count,"a":[{"p":[lon,lat],"g":[[[lon,lat],...],...],"l":["401 North 27th Street","..."]}, ...]} where p is the dot point, g the rings and l the deduplicated address lines (city and zip in a second field when they differ from the tile's most common); footprints with no address have "l": []; unmatched address points are written into the same shard's "u": [[lon,lat,"line","city","zip","placement letter"],...] so the browser draws them as dots too (D15, D32), and per D28 the module rewrites hail/a/ so its shards hold only the unmatched rows (the search index keeps every row; verify checks that every address row appears exactly once across b/ lists and a/ shards); (5) index.json gains "buildings": {state, source (file name, size, date, the attribution "Oak Ridge National Laboratory and FEMA, USA Structures" and the licence reading from the brief: Data.gov lists U.S. government works; the hosted copy CC BY 4.0; to be confirmed with FEMA), counts (footprints 918,052 expected; multipart; with addresses inside; within 15 m; without; unmatched points by placement class; per county the outline count beside the address count, D34), shards, bytes, largest shard, depth histogram} and a counts file hail/counts.json with one building count per B1 tile for the zoom 13 and 14 bubbles (D27) with manifest entries; the unavailable state per D20; (6) WORDS_BUILDINGS per D29, D32 and D34: the legend line "Each dot is one building outline. Tap a dot for its address, if one is on file, and the weather history for its cell.", the sheet's lines ("No address on file for this building. The weather history below is for this building's cell.", "Units on file: {n}.", the address list header, the placement sentence "This address point was placed {how}, not on the building." with the five {how} phrases of D32), the count bubble template ("{n} buildings"), the About lines ("Building outlines: USA Structures, Oak Ridge National Laboratory and FEMA (file dated 2026-09-13). Outlines come from imagery and are not surveys." and "Outlines come from imagery dated 2008 to 2025 and are not surveys; sheds and barns are outlines too."), the unavailable sentence, D23's outside-the-grid sentence if a footprint's tile has no B1 shard; the forbidden-word test for these templates covers home, house, residence, dwelling and use, with "structure" allowed only inside the two proper names (D29); describe_buildings(index) and map_data_buildings(index) (state, counts, the shard URL pattern, the split map, the zoom thresholds of D27: counts bubbles at 13 and 14, dots from 15, fills and hairlines from 16, outline emphasis at 17; the dot radius rule, the tap radius 12 px, every template); (7) verify: counts; every footprint ring has at least 4 points and closes; every address row is either in a footprint's l or in a shard's u exactly once and the rewritten a/ holds exactly the u rows (no row lost, none doubled; D28); outline dots equal footprints; the Billings box figures against the research (307 footprints intersect the box 45.78 to 45.79 N, 108.51 to 108.50 W; 535 of 869 points inside, 313 within 15 m, 21 farther; 131 footprints with no point inside; all 869 are Structure-placed, so the box cannot exercise D32: add a Sanders County box where most points are Geocoding-placed and record its counts); every shard within the byte cap unless at the depth cap; the counts file sums to the footprint total; manifest hashes; (8) the CLI build|verify with --store, --cache, --gdb-zip; (9) tests with a synthetic geodatabase-free path: the module's join and shard code is tested on in-memory polygons and points (a tiny fixture of rings) so the tests need no pyogrio; the reader is tested with pyogrio only when it imports (skipUnless) on a small zip the test writes with pyogrio.write_dataframe if available, else skipped; the forbidden-attribute assertion; the words check. Then RUN the real build: wait for ${OUT}/streets/hail-store.tar.gz (poll every 2 minutes up to 60 minutes; else use ${STORE_TAR}) and tar it into ${OUT}/buildings/store; download the FEMA file into ${FOOT_DIR} if missing (one HEAD and one GET, ledger); ${VENV} -m website.buildings build --store ${OUT}/buildings/store --gdb-zip ${FOOT_DIR}/MT_Structures_20260913.zip; verify; measure wall time (the research read 918,052 features statewide), shards, bytes of b/ and of the rewritten a/, the largest shard, the depth histogram, the join counts statewide (inside, within 15 m, unmatched points by placement class, footprints without addresses, outside-the-grid tiles; the research expects about 81,800 unmatched rows and about 5.3 MB in a/); a second build byte-identical; tar as ${OUT}/buildings/hail-store.tar.gz for the site; the job step per D20 with its timeout.`

const SITE = `${COMMON}

You are the site builder. You own website/build.py, website/sources.py, website/templates/ (map.html, about.html; town.html only if needed), tests/test_site.py, tools/smoke_map.py and .github/workflows/website.yml. The streets and buildings builders are writing website/streets.py and website/buildings.py now with the public API fixed above (WORDS_*, describe_*(index), map_data_*(index), the shard formats); website/addresses.py already exists with WORDS_ADDRESSES, describe_addresses(index) and map_data_addresses(index). Poll every 2 minutes (up to 60 minutes) for the new modules before your integration tests; build the templates, the flags and the smoke checks from the brief meanwhile. Build: (1) build.py: the second default-off flag --hail-addresses (an error without --hail-history); with it copy hail/a/, hail/r/ and hail/b/ from the store into the site (include them in the manifest check), add map.json["hail"]["addresses"], ["roads"] and ["buildings"] from the three map_data functions, render the About terms paragraphs from the three describe functions (D13, D17, D29, D34: the law citation to MCA 2-6-1017 only; the three attribution lines for the sources built; the quoted constraints; the accuracy caveats; the privacy sentence; the no-owner sentence; the imagery-dates sentence), the "Find an address" form and the legend lines on the Map page, and the attribution lines on the map's first screen (Leaflet's attribution control carries the building and streets lines, D29); the option --address-text off (D35): dots carry no address text and no search index or form is written, so the smoke runs once in each mode; without the flag nothing of B3 appears: the flag-off build (both flags off) stays byte-identical to the base except shared static assets and their ?v= hashes, and a --hail-history build without --hail-addresses is byte-identical to the same build from the base; a store whose roads or buildings part is unavailable still builds, with the unavailable sentences; (2) sources.py: three CONTRACTS rows: msl_addresses (per the brief's Product and D3, D4, D22: cadence monthly export; positions converted at 5 decimals; the missing rules; the terms quotes; the coverage caveat without numbers), msl_roads (the Library file; its use sentence quoted; the classes; the merge and simplification rules; the named share in words) and census_roads (TIGER 2026; the acknowledgement; the vehicular classes; the merge and simplification rules; the unnamed share in words; the accuracy caveat; the trademark note), of which the About page shows the one built, usa_structures (the file date; geometry only; the attribution and licence reading; the join rules 15 m and the placement classes of D32; the imagery caveat; "building outline" words), gated like hail_history; (3) templates: map.html gains the form (text input, results list, the privacy sentence), the legend lines for dots, streets and shapes (words from the modules through map.json or the template), rendered only with the flag; about.html the terms paragraphs with the flag; (4) tools/smoke_map.py gains --addresses on a build that has them, with the synthesis's smoke scope (D30): at zoom 12 over Billings no road, outline, counts or address shard is fetched; at zoom 13 arterials and the count bubbles appear and no footprint shard is fetched; at zoom 15 local streets, one dot per outline and the unmatched address dots appear; at 16 fills, hairlines and street names; the fetch budget for a 390 px Billings view at zoom 15 is under 650 KB gzip (measure it); draw time under 30 ms per redraw at 15 and 16; pan across Billings at zoom 15 and count fetches (list them; expect under 20; all on-site); tap an outline's dot: the sheet shows its address lines on top (or the no-address sentence, with no address lines), then the hail days and the six B2 sections; tap an unmatched address dot: the address line on top and the placement sentence; the attribution lines are visible on the first screen at 390 px; search "401 N 27th St Billings" (that address listed and opened), "27th Billings" (a list), "Colony Rd Roundup" (rows), "qwzx 99" (the no-match sentence); the typed text appears in no request URL; the streets' names appear from zoom 16 (count labels drawn through the page hook); the same run with the --address-text off build shows dots without address text and no form; --shots at 390x844 and 1280x800 on the white map and Imagery; (5) tests/test_site.py: the flag plumbing and error, the identity checks, the three contract rows, the map.js literal scan (no sentence, unit, radius, zoom threshold, cap, class width or colour literal), the templates with and without the flag, the About terms only with the flag, the unavailable states, the --address-text off mode, the forbidden-word test over every B3 template (home, house, residence, dwelling, use; "structure" only in the proper names); (6) website.yml: previews pass --hail-addresses with --hail-history and run smoke_map with --addresses; the test step runs tests.test_streets and tests.test_buildings. Build and check: ${VENV} -m unittest tests.test_site; builds: flag-off --sample --now 2026-10-19T12:00:00Z into ${OUT}/site/off; --hail-history --sample into ${OUT}/site/history (compare with the same build from the base archive); --hail-history --hail-addresses --sample into ${OUT}/site/sample (the fixture has a/; r/ and b/ fixture shards come from the module builders' fixture writers if they add them, else the sample build must show the unavailable sentences for roads and shapes); when ${OUT}/buildings/hail-store.tar.gz exists (poll every 3 minutes up to 90 minutes) --hail-history --hail-addresses --sample --hail-store that tar into ${OUT}/site/real (and once more with --address-text off into ${OUT}/site/real-notext) and run PW_CHROMIUM=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium ${VENV} tools/smoke_map.py --addresses --shots on both. Report what you changed and measured.`

const BROWSER = `${COMMON}

You are the browser builder. You own website/static/map/map.js and website/static/map/map.css only. Read map.js in full first (its header documents every browser-only duty; the hail sheet code shows the fetch, cache and template-fill pattern), then the rendering research record ${RESEARCH}/rendering.json (zoom thresholds, canvas costs, label rule) and the B3 brief's D5 to D7, D14 to D16a and D25 to D35 (the thresholds of D27 and the counts layer; the name table of D26; the unmatched rows and their placement letter of D28 and D32; the no-address-text mode of D35). Build, as documented duties in the header: (1) a canvas overlay layer (one canvas pane positioned by Leaflet, redrawn on move and zoom end, drawing order streets, then shapes, then dots) that at zooms 13 and 14 fetches hail/counts.json once and draws one count bubble per B1 tile ("{n} buildings" from the template) and the arterial classes of the road shards whose bounds intersect the viewport, from zoom 15 the local streets, the building shards and the address shards (unmatched rows only), and from zoom 16 the fills, hairlines and names (D27), each named from map.json's split maps by the B1 cell-to-tile arithmetic plus the quadrant digits; fetched shards are cached in memory (a size cap from map.json; least recently used eviction); every request is on-site; (2) drawing: streets as polylines with the stroke width per class from map.json and colour tokens from map.css (CSS variables read once), names (from the shard's name table) from zoom 16 along the longest piece of each distinct name per tile with a grid collision check, in the small type; outlines as a light fill with a hairline from 16 and the outline emphasis at 17; dots: from zoom 15 one dot per outline at its dot point and the unmatched address dots (their placement letter kept for the sheet); nothing below 15 but the count bubbles and arterials; dot radius 2.5 px at zoom 13 to 4 px at 16 and above; a hazard-free dot colour token; (3) the tap: the nearest dot within the tap radius (map.json) opens the hail sheet for that dot's cell with the address lines on top (the outline's list with the units line, or the single address with its placement sentence when the letter is not Structure, or the no-address sentence; in the --address-text off mode no address text at all), then B1's hail days and B2's six sections; a tile with no hail shard shows D23's sentence; (4) the search per D6: normalise with words.json (abbreviations expanded), take a leading number, find the city as the longest trailing match against cities.json, pick the core-name token, fetch the city's key file (one or two characters), list rows whose normalised street contains every typed non-number token, exact number first then nearest numbers, up to the cap; choosing a row zooms to its point at zoom 17 and opens its sheet; the no-match and unavailable sentences from the templates; (5) states: an unavailable roads, buildings or addresses part draws nothing for that part and the legend line says so (the sentence from map.json); a failed shard fetch is logged in the page hook and never throws; (6) a page hook (window object the smoke reads: shards loaded per kind, dots drawn, labels drawn, last fetch list) documented as test-only; (7) no literal sentence, unit, radius, zoom threshold, cap, class width or colour in map.js (formatting constants allowed); map.css adds the tokens and the form and results list styles in the field-sheet style (docs/DESIGN.md), light and dark. Test in Chromium yourself on the site builder's builds under ${OUT}/site/ as they appear (poll every 3 minutes up to 90 minutes; read tools/smoke_map.py's harness), measuring: shards fetched and bytes gzip for a 390 px Billings view at zoom 15 (budget 650 KB), draw milliseconds per redraw over Billings at zooms 13, 15, 16 and 17 (budget 30 ms at 15 and 16 on a 1280x800 canvas), the label count at 16, the fetch count when panning, and that a zoom 13 view fetches no footprint shard. Report the measurements and the header text you added.`

reviews.summary: Read-only review of claude/hail-b3 for the daily job and the budget. The three B3 store steps (roads, addresses, outlines) run end to end in workflow order on empty caches, with every step exiting 0, and their outputs are byte-identical to the builders' store: r/ 4,427, b/ 5,615 and a/ 11,714 files, and counts.json. One blocking defect: the enlarged archive (31,129 files, 372.7 MB under hail/) is refused by the site's own unpack limits (hail.py:789-790: 20,000 files, 300 MiB), so every branch Website build that loads the release with --hail-history fails --require-live; main is unaffected. Measured budget: the B3 steps take 14.1 min on this VM and the full job about 26 min (about 24 min without download waits) against the 25-min gate, and the daily rebuild of roads and outlines, which the synthesis planned monthly or annual, is the avoidable cost. Cache: warm runs are HEAD-only (4.7 s, zero GETs), but the outline cache holds a 334 MB extracted geodatabase, so each daily run restores about 702 MB. Failure paths: a blocked network passes for roads, addresses and outlines. A real SIGTERM during the roads shard write leaves hail/.r-stage, which makes addresses verify, buildings verify and the site's manifest check fail. YAML parses with no double equals; the push paths omit streets.py and buildings.py; two unavailable steps lack continue-on-error; the non-fatal caps sum to 105 minutes against a 90-minute job. Browser: a phone view at zoom 15 over Billings is 618,308 B with three font faces (651,525 B with all six), under the 650 KiB gate, but the smoke enforces only the 267,801 B of B3 files; data/map.json is 73 KB gzip, mostly repeated tile lists; the overhang pad is not applied; zoom 13 fetches 94% local-street vertices. 10-minute site: the flag-on site is 377 MB; tar extract, copy and manifest check take about 9 s warm, far under the 15-minute Website timeout, and the unpack refusal is the real constraint. The data-site split would leave main's build unchanged (it already skips the store) and would move the 373 MB out of the preview path, at the cost of a second Pages deploy at 37% of the 1 GB limit and an untested 10-minute deploy. The dot-shard total is 203.8 MB against the 60 MB target in D38, which needs an owner decision. Not measured here: the B1 hail build and joins, runner network and disk speed, Pages deploy time, the Chromium smoke, and the 3G target, which the repo does not define.

If none exists, keep the rounded dot and count it as an exception. (2) In verify (lines 1057-1069), test the stored rounded dot against the stored rounded rings with the same exact test, not der.edge_* and not float parity. Report dots_outside_outline (expect 0) and the exception count as its own key (expect 11), and correct the comment. (3) Tests: a footprint whose centroid rounds onto an edge ends up strictly inside; a footprint one unit tall is counted as an exception; on a synthetic store the verify counts equal the exact counts. Change what the Douglas-Peucker check measures: each removed point is measured to the segment between the stored positions of its two kept neighbours, not the source positions. (1) Add a helper _stored_metres(net, x, y, np): the build's own round trip, with dst = LIBRARY_LONLAT if net.kind == 'msl' else TIGER_GEO, lon, lat = _forward_inverse(net.crs, dst, x, y), then return _forward_inverse(dst, net.crs, np.rint(lon * SCALE) / SCALE, np.rint(lat * SCALE) / SCALE). (2) In the clean_network loop (lines 1089-1092) compute sx, sy = _stored_metres(net, px, py, np) for each piece and call _dp_keep(px, py, DP_TOL_M, np, sx, sy). A per-piece call gives bitwise the same stored positions as one batched call. Rejected: DP_TOL_M = 1.3 is a valid bound (1.3 plus the rounding displacement is under 2.0; sample max 1.82 m), but it changes a decided number, adds about 18 percent vertices in the sample, and resizes every shard, so it is neither minimal nor within the decisions.
